text: A partner panel change is published by rwb-access as a door and a record: the workbook of the panel rows is handed unchanged to the reference-load operation of rwb-case with the table code partner_panel and validFrom, and rwb-access stores no partner row, no panel status, no reference row and no rule row of its own.
why: FEAT-PRM-02 is held as versioned reference data by S9 and, under the R-PREC default ruling, reference data and its loads are P3 rwb-case's, while the context pack gives rwb-access five tables and none of them is a partner or reference table, so the access service can only own the operation, the authority check, the hand-over and the record.
read: FEAT-PRM-02 and FEAT-ADM-07 in the Epics 3 to 8 specification; ASM-A6-tables-5 and ASM-A6-api-4; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.23.2; context pack P4 ownership rows; Template and Rules R3.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case (P3) as the owner of the reference data, and the partner and agency manager as the business owner of the panel
impact: If the panel rows must stay with the partner service instead, only the consumed operation and its owner change from rwb-case to rwb-partner; the change, its record and its effective dating stay as they are.

text: The effective date of a panel change is data and not a job: validFrom is carried to the owner's load, the version is in force from that date and not before it, and rwb-access registers no Schedule and no workflow to activate a change; its one job is JOB-18, the six-monthly access review, and it owns no workflow.
why: R-UNI-38 applies a version from its effective date, the technical specification gives every versioned table its valid-from and valid-to dates, and the context pack gives the service one job and no workflow, so a timer in the access service would be a second clock over another service's data.
read: R-UNI-38; REQ-DRI-011; context pack P4 ownership rows (jobs 1, workflows 0); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 valid_from columns; Template and Rules R5.5 DP table.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case (P3) and the platform workflow owner
impact: If a promotion job is required after all, it is a DP-10 change with H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON in a later story; this change and its record do not move.

text: The rule version a panel change names is read from the P7 rule-package contract and its fake, and the publish accepts only a version in state APPROVED or IN_FORCE whose valid-from date is not after the effective date of the change; the legacy rule-version endpoints are the registry's and the missing C dependency is raised at D1 rather than added to the metadata.
why: The legacy story's two endpoints are the rule package registry's under ASM-A6-api-3 and the legacy precondition says the rule version the feature needs must be in place, while the metadata contract-dependency list of this key carries only RWB-P3-E1042-CON, so the read has to be declared as consumed against the registry's contract and its fake.
read: RWB-E8-012 story, endpoints and AC1; ASM-A6-api-3; TSD P4 v3 T3.2, T4 and T6.3; Temporal and Drools design slide 15.
impact: If the registry exposes a read by version id instead of the package version list, only the consumed path changes; the accepted states and the refusal stay as they are.

text: A published panel change is recorded as one entry of the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library, written under the library's administrative-change record code with the change id, the partner type, the panel version, the load id, the effective date, the rule id and version, the parameters version and the caller reference; the central ledger decision_log_entry stays with rwb-decision and is neither read nor written here.
why: R-UNI-39 requires no action to proceed unlogged, the legacy criterion puts the result in the decision log with the rule version, and the context pack gives rwb-access no ledger, so the entry is the service's own chain and the central view remains the decision service's.
read: R-UNI-39; RWB-E8-012 AC1 and AC2; DP-03; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 decision-log linkage; context pack P4 ownership rows.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-decision (P7) as the owner of the ledger view and the library owner
impact: If the library publishes a distinct code for a reference-data publish, only the entry code changes and the fields of the answer stay as the contract fixes them.

text: The change has one state of its own, PUBLISHED, fixed by the contract; the state of the load and the accepted state of the rule version are drawn from LOV-VERSION-STATUS of the module specification, and inForce is computed from the effective date against the date of the read rather than stored.
why: The sources give a lifecycle for a rule package version and a list of version states, and no state for an administrative change or for a reference load, so the change needs one stated value and every other state has to come from the owner through the only closed set the module specification provides.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.2 and T4; FSD P4 v3 A2.23.4; R-UNI-38; RWB-E8-012 AC1.
confirm: Audit representative and the tech lead of rwb-case (P3)
impact: If a change must show the approval of its load as a state of its own, one value is added to the closed set in a reviewed contract change; the record and the answer fields do not move.

text: The screen that carries a panel change is SCR-40 Reference data, served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19; the legacy story's SCR-39 Rules and parameters and SCR-41 Delegation of authority carry no panel and get no panel field from this story.
why: The legacy story names two screens that hold rule versions and approval limits, the module specification lists SCR-40 Reference data for lists of values and reference tables with versions, and a panel is versioned reference data, so the change belongs on the reference-data screen.
read: RWB-E8-012 screen and states; FSD P4 v3 Screens and A2.23.2; DP-19; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1.
confirm: Tech lead of the gateway-bff contract (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and the reference data administrator
impact: If the change must sit on SCR-39 or on a new screen, only section 15 and the route stub change; the operations and the record do not.

text: A publish whose decision-record entry cannot be written is compensated by the owner's rollback of the load it just created, and answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no change id; where the rollback also fails the load stays LOADED and unapproved, the 503 names the load id and one incident is raised, so nothing is in force either way.
why: The legacy criterion says that where the decision log cannot be written nothing changes, and the module specification says the incident is raised; the load is created before the record because the record states the load id, so the order has to be made good by a compensation.
read: RWB-E8-012 AC2; FSD P4 v3 A2.23.4.3 AC-EXC-P4-023-02; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 API-P4-010 rollback; DP-03.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-case (P3) and the operations owner of the record store
impact: If the owner prefers a load that is withdrawn only by its own approval path, the compensation call changes and the answer and the incident stay as they are.

text: The publish needs Reference data C and the read needs Reference data R; the legacy story's Rules and parameters C and A are mapped under the R-PREC order, where the technical specification wins, so the A letter sits with the approval of the load on the console path and with the approval of the rule version in the registry and never with this operation.
why: The legacy permission table and the technical specification disagree on the capability area and on the role that holds the right, and R-PREC resolves the disagreement in favour of the technical specification; the gap is recorded as a conflict so the matrix can be corrected as data rather than as a release.
read: RWB-E8-012 permission checks; TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.23.3.3; Template and Rules R3.
confirm: Security administrator and the business owner of the partner panel
impact: If the matrix must keep Rules and parameters C for the publish, one permission letter and one sentence of the authority section change; no field, record or operation moves.

text: The contract slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion, so it writes its own contract test set TC-E8-012-CON-01 to -06 at Level Contract, and the four legacy test case ids stay with the app slice RWB-P4-E8012-APP and, for AC1, with the integration slice RWB-ITG-E8012-ITG, whose -ITG copies are written on that story; no -ITG copy is minted here.
why: The acs list of the contract story is empty while its tcs_legacy list carries the four ids of the key, and item 5 of the Work Package keeps the legacy ids of the criteria a story owns and gives an integration copy the -ITG suffix, so restating the four ids here would give one test case two owners.
read: _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-012.md (the RWB-P4-E8012-CON line, acs empty with four tcs_legacy entries); RWB-E8-012 test case table; RWB ITG E8012 ITG Publish a panel change - integration v1.md section 16; Template and Rules R7.2 s16.
applied_in: RWB-P4-E8012-CON section 16 and the tcs array of _work/msr/fragments/RWB-P4-E8012-CON.json; RWB-P4-E8012-APP section 16
confirm: QA lead at test review, with the rwb-access tech lead
impact: If the legacy ids are required in the contract story too, six rows are added to its section 16 and six entries to its fragment; no acceptance criterion, contract table or message changes.
